newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand fell back sharply on Wednesday in a mirror-image of Tuesday's roller-coaster ride as speculators took advantage of the currency's strength to establish fresh bear positions.
"This morning we saw lots of unwinding of long dollar positions with exporters coming in strongly," said one trader.
"Now that's all gone out of the window and offshore players are buying dollars again. I'd say we're going to test 4.70 tomorrow."
The first decisive exporter demand for rand in weeks saw the rand firm to 4.64 against the dollar in early trade on Wednesday as a rally which started late Tuesday snowballed.

But the advance was capped by demand for the U.S. unit from local importers, and by mid-afternoon offshore banks were taking up fresh speculative positions as the rand probed the 4.6850 support level.
Analysts said the rand's rally had triggered a lot of stops among dollar longs but now players were looking to buy the dollar on dips.
"There's been a bit of a shakeout and I would now expect people to start looking to buy dollars on the dips," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
"Sentiment is very much that the trend depreciation in the currency is still as much in place as it ever was."

Bonds initially took heart from the rand's early advance with the yield on the benchmark R150 nosing back below 16 percent briefly after kicking up to a five-month high of 16.24 at one stage on Tuesday.

Dealers reported some early local institutional demand for bonds but the market was knocked lower by the weaker rand and the continued squeeze at the short end of the market, exacerbated by news of a sharp jump in Tuesday's money market shortage to nearly 10 billion rand.
"The problem is that with money market rates remaining so high they (institutions) are not prepared to put too much into gilts," said one.
The rand was last at 4.6830/80 against dollar from 4.6785/35 on Tuesday. Against the crosses, it was at 7.7373/7502 from 7.7092/7222 against sterling and at 0.3212/16 marks against 0.3201/06.
The R150 long bond was last at 16.10 percent from 16.09.
Foreigners bought a net 51.08 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying a net 79.04 million rand on Monday, the Bond Exchange said on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 3.98 billion rand on Tuesday from 5.93 billion rand on Monday.
Commercial banks held their three-month NCD rates steady at between 16.85 and 17.10 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was unchanged at 16.25 to 16.45 percent.
The daily money market shortage for Tuesday was 9.810 billion rand from Monday's 9.110 billion.
